answer: Use latency triangulation. Each epoch, five verifier nodes on different continents send an agent a fresh nonce and time its signed reply. The round-trip times form a rough fingerprint of where its machine sits, whether a rack beside a lagoon or a box near a summit. Identities whose fingerprints match within a few milliseconds share one reward cap. To make 50 fakes look distinct, an attacker must rent servers in 50 separate regions and keep them all online every epoch, turning cheap clones into a heavy, ferrous hosting bill that recurs forever.
